newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen up in coming week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen up in coming week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are expected to jump in the upcoming trading week on increased demand in the local market and higher prices of the commodity abroad, dealers said on Saturday.

"The 27-day long strike of edible oil tankers has finally ended and there is heavy vegoil oil demand in the local market," a dealer at Jaleel Brothers Ltd said. "In the international market the price trend is upward on an increased demand from European and other countries."
Dealers said vegoil stocks rose to an estimated 208,500 tonnes last week from 194,500 tonnes a week back. RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks rose to 175,000 tonnes compared with 165,000 last week.
Soybean oil and Sunflower oil stocks rose to 20,000 from 16,000 tonnes. The Ghee Corporation of Pakistan's (GCP) palm oil and palm olien stocks remained steady at 13,500 tonnes.
Dealers said the GCP booked 6,000 tonnes palm oil last month.
Bunga Selasih is discharging an estimated 11,987 tonnes of palm oil at the Karachi Port, while Wawasan Courage with around 25,270 tonnes of palm oil is at the outer anchorage.
Sielo-Di-Milona with an estimated 12,000 soybean oil is expected to arrive in the second week of January.
Wawasan Murni and Wawasan Megah will load palm oil for Pakistan in January at a Malaysian port.
